LESSON: CAPA CITY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.3: Capa city
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capa city, part of Measurement in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How can we find out which of two containers hold more, less or the same as?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign capacity and terms related to capacity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capa city in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. collect containers of different capacities from the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capa city in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. compare capacity of two containers using more than, less than and same as,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capa city in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. measure capacity using arbitrary units,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capa city in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. re-use empty containers of different capacities to keep items,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capa city in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. play digital games involving capacity. • In pairs, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign terms related to capacity such as capacity, more than, less than. • In groups learners are guided to collect safe containers of different sizes from the environment. • Learners in pairs or groups empty and fill water in different containers to establish which holds more, which holds less, and which holds the same. • Learners in pairs or groups carefully fill basins with water, using different small containers. • The learners in groups count the number of small containers they use to fill the basin. • Learners in pairs or groups to be guided to discuss and re-use containers of different capacity at home and school. How can we find out which of two containers hold more, less or the same as? ● Peace: harmoniously sing by signing songs or rhymes related to days of the week, months and year together.

Patriotism as learner identifies activities that take place during the days of the week such as raising flag on Monday and Friday.
